ole in the system).
2. Remembers "what the tree looked like last time" via **content hashes + a mani

fest**, so the next

overable transaction**; retiring a document is an explicit, evidence-gated

saction**; retiring a document is an explicit, evidence-gated

The stance, in one sentence: **"docs are in sync" must be backed by a manifest the tooling wrote,
no
t by the model that produced the prose.**

## Repository layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## The two problems it solves
| # | Problem | What this repo gives you |
| **1** | You want to map an unfamiliar codebase quickly, and keep a baseline for "what changed sinc
e" | **Outline**: `project_docs/**/*.md`, one document per source directory. **Baseline**: `_scan_st
ate.json` (per-file SHA-256 + directory fingerprints) plus the manifest's `generation_id` (content-o

nly hash). Together they make the next sync **incremental** instead of a full rewrite. |
| **2** | Y
ou want a new AI conversation to load the project shape instead of re-reading source from scratch |
**The loader ships in this repo**: `tools/load_docs.py` first verifies the manifest against the docu
ments (per-file hashes + complete-set check), then serves either an **overview** (tree + metadata +
section names) or a **single document / single section**. Writer and reader import the same contract
, so the rules cannot drift apart. |
Why not just "have a model write a pile of `.md` files"? Because **the producer and the verifier mus

t
be separate actors** — otherwise "the model says it's in sync" can never be falsified.
| Failure mode | Symptom | What this tool does |
| Drift | Source gained a file; the document's inventory is permanently one row short | Content-hash

snapshot + worklist; only changed directories are rewritten |
| Unfalsifiable claims | "It's synced
" with nothing to check | An independent manifest records size/SHA-256/title/status per document; mi

smatch is refused |
| Mass rewrite destroys history | Everything is rewritten just to pass validatio
n | Only documents for changed directories block; unchanged history is audited, not rewritten |
## Guarantees
| Guarantee | Mechanism |
| **No writes by default** | Without `--apply` everything is report-only; staging lives in the syste

m temp dir, never in the project tree |
| **Single commit point** | The atomic replace of `project_d

ocs/_manifest.json` is the only documentation-generation commit point |
| **Never clobbers concurren
t writes** | Publication uses no-replace rename (Windows `os.rename`, Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPL

ACE)`); a mismatched preimage aborts |
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations and trade-offs

- Journal and CAS artifact directories must live on **the same filesystem** as the project root
(cro

ss-volume setups make `--apply` refuse).
- Path whitelist: relative POSIX, lowercase `.md` only; abs

olute paths, drive letters, backslashes,
`..`, ADS, reserved device names and case-only conflicts ar

e rejected.
- **Symlinks, junctions and reparse points are never followed**; when path identity cann

ot be proven,
the tool fails closed.
- `--full` is only the scanner's `force_full` switch — it is **

not** "reconcile every document's file
inventory"; that remains a producer step.
- Document retireme

nt is a **burden-of-proof flow**, not a cleanup utility: report-only by default,
`--apply` requires
explicit authorization.
